title: Off the Mark
intro: Getting to the ball on time starts with your first two steps, and you can train them. Every start here is one you choose, so go flat out and take the full rest after each one. It's sixteen starts, about ninety-two metres of running in all. If you haven't done any jump work lately, do Landing Gear first, because every split-step here is a landing.

You need a court or about twenty-five metres of flat, non-slip ground, and court shoes. Mark each distance with tape or a line, not cones or bags you could step on. Run through the end of every start and slow down over the next ten metres. Do it on fresh legs early in the day, never as a finisher. If your starts get slower than the ones before, end the session there.

before.label: Not today
before.text: A sore ankle, knee, calf, hamstring, groin or Achilles, or an injury in the last month? Get it looked at first.

before.label: Stop and get it checked
before.text: A sharp pain, pain that spreads, numbness, swelling, a joint that gives way, or a sudden pull or pop.

before.label: Stop now
before.text: Chest pain, dizziness, a heartbeat that races or skips, or breathing that doesn't feel right. Get it looked at before you train again. Told to be careful with hard exercise? Check with your doctor first.

before.label: Past injury
before.text: Ever torn a knee ligament, or coming back from an ankle injury? Ask whoever treated you if starts and cuts are OK.

before.label: Keep clear
before.text: 48 hours away from another hard session, and not the day before a match.

before.label: First time
before.text: Do two sets of each start instead of four.
